principles.statement: For penalty-aware TSP with carrot constraint (N=200K, 2s), grid-guided 2-opt with penalty-aware exact delta + Or-opt + pos[] tracking + continuous SA outperforms random swap + approximate boundary-only 2-opt by ~9.3 points (78.85 vs 69.5). The critical enabler is grid-based spatial neighbor lookup (O(1), reusing the NN construction grid) which avoids expensive KNN precomputation.
principles.mechanism: Grid-guided 2-opt finds improving segment reversals by looking up spatial neighbors through the same grid used for NN construction. Penalty-aware exact delta computation (iterating over 10th-step positions in the reversed segment) ensures moves respect the penalty structure. Or-opt (single-city relocation with bounded shift) provides additional diversification. The pos[] array enables O(1) lookup of a city's tour position for guiding 2-opt endpoints. Combined, these produce ~9.3 points more than random swap SA because they make spatially-informed, penalty-correct moves.
principles.applicability_bounds: Requires N large enough that random moves are unlikely to find nearby cities. The grid granularity (G=sqrt(N)) balances spatial resolution with cell population.

principles.statement: REVISION: The penalty structure contributes significantly (>6 points) when penalty-aware delta computation is combined with Or-opt and prime scheduling at the iter-2 level of algorithmic sophistication. The prior claim that penalty contributes 'at most ~1%' was measured on iter-1's simpler algorithm where the SA wasn't exploiting penalty structure. At higher tour quality levels, penalty-aware moves become more important because distance-based improvements are harder to find.
principles.regime: Penalty-aware TSP, N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, high-quality tours
principles.mechanism: At high tour quality, most edge swaps have similar distance costs. Penalty-aware delta computation lets the SA distinguish moves that also reduce penalty charges, finding improvements invisible to distance-only evaluation. Or-opt moves cities into prime-aligned positions. Prime scheduling post-pass reorders to minimize non-prime penalties on every-10th steps.
principles.applicability_bounds: This revision applies at the quality level of the iter-2 solution (~78.8). At iter-1's quality level (~69.5), penalty-aware computation may still contribute only ~1% because distance improvements dominate.

principles.statement: For penalty-aware TSP under tight time limits (2s, N=200K), grid-guided spatial neighbor selection for 2-opt (using G=sqrt(N) grid, O(1) per lookup) outperforms both precomputed KNN lists (O(N*K) build overhead causes timing variance) and random selection, because it provides spatial guidance without startup cost. Verified: grid-guided scores ~78.85 consistently, KNN-based is timing-sensitive and scores 64.5-78.8 depending on N.
principles.regime: N >= 50000, 2s time limit, grid-NN construction available
principles.mechanism: The grid is already built for NN construction (free). Looking up a city's spatial neighbors is O(1) — select a random cell within radius 2, pick a random city from that cell. KNN precomputation (O(N*K)) takes 0.3-0.5s for N=200K, K=20, which is 15-25% of the time budget and causes high score variance.
principles.applicability_bounds: Grid lookup works well when cities are distributed roughly uniformly. For highly clustered distributions, the grid cells may be very uneven.

principles.statement: Double-bridge perturbation (non-sequential 4-opt) does NOT improve TSP score within a 2-second time limit for N=200K, even with grid-guided 2-opt. ILS with double-bridge (mean 75.7, high variance) underperforms continuous SA without perturbation (mean 78.85, low variance). The O(N) tour recomputation after each perturbation plus shorter SA phases with cold restarts outweighs the benefit of escaping local optima.
principles.mechanism: Double-bridge creates a non-sequential 4-opt perturbation that disrupts the tour structure. For N=200K, rebuilding the tour quality after perturbation requires significant SA time. With only 2s total, ILS manages 2-3 restarts with cold temperature resets, each producing shorter SA phases that can't fully recover. Continuous SA invests all time in a single long anneal, reaching a better final solution.
principles.applicability_bounds: May not apply with longer time budgets (10s+) where ILS has time for more restarts and full recovery after perturbation.

principles.statement: Multi-city Or-opt (segments 1-3) with grid-guided insertion does not measurably improve score beyond single-city Or-opt for penalty-aware TSP at N=200K within 2s. The effect, if present, is below 0.2 points (~0.25% of score).
principles.regime: N >= 50000, 2s time limit, grid-guided SA with Or-opt
principles.mechanism: Single-city Or-opt (relocate one city by small shift) is fast (O(shift) for memmove + O(shift) for pos[] update). Multi-city Or-opt (relocate segments of 2-3) has higher memmove cost and more complex delta computation. For N=200K, the throughput reduction from handling segments outweighs the quality improvement from moving coherent groups.
principles.applicability_bounds: Based on bounded-shift Or-opt (shift <= 15). Unbounded Or-opt was not tested due to throughput concerns.

principles.statement: Two-phase grid-guided 2-opt SA without penalty-aware delta, Or-opt, or prime scheduling scores only ~72.2 for penalty-aware TSP (N=200K, 2s) — a 6.6-point regression from the iter-2 cumulative solution (78.8) that includes all three. The missing components (penalty-aware exact delta, Or-opt relocation, prime scheduling) contribute ~6.6 points collectively, confirming they are essential, not marginal optimizations.
principles.regime: Penalty-aware TSP, N up to 200K, 2-second time limit
principles.mechanism: Grid-guided 2-opt alone provides spatial candidate selection but without penalty-aware delta computation, the SA accepts/rejects moves based on distance-only cost estimates that ignore the 10% surcharge on non-prime sourced edges. Or-opt handles city relocations that 2-opt cannot express (single-city moves to better positions). Prime scheduling reorders the final tour to minimize non-prime penalties. Each missing component degrades score.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies when comparing grid-guided 2-opt approaches with vs without penalty-aware delta + Or-opt + prime scheduling. The 6.6-point gap is specific to this problem's penalty structure.
